summary.description: Hydrogen chloride is a colourless, chemically reactive gas with a strong odour. When in contact with water, it forms hydrochloric acid (HCl).
emission_sources: Waste incinerators, especially those burning plastic PVC
environmental_impact: Highly corrosive, leading to damage of metals and limestone
Contributes to the corrosion of buildings and cultural monuments
Accidental large discharges can significantly harm aquatic ecosystems

top_sdg_impacts.SDG6_Clean_Water_and_Sanitation: Large accidental discharges of hydrogen chloride into water bodies can harm aquatic ecosystems, affecting water quality and the sustainability of clean water systems.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG11_Sustainable_Cities_and_Communities: Hydrogen chloride is highly corrosive and contributes to the degradation of infrastructure, buildings, and cultural monuments, impacting the sustainability and heritage of urban areas.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG14_Life_Below_Water: When released into water, hydrogen chloride can severely affect aquatic life due to its high acidity, disrupting ecosystems and harming marine biodiversity.
